decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures issuance, eligibility, and reset rules but omits that the Small Block counter operates independently from the Big Block counter.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I have one final-final adjustment to the mechanics that should make everything cleaner and easier to code, without any strange half-expiring tickets.
This new rule replaces the earlier ticket lifespan description:
→ Whenever someone mints using a referral code, the referrer immediately receives two distinct tickets on their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

The two counters operate completely independently.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Only Small Block Tickets issued after the previous small block are eligible for the draw.
Once the draw is complete, burn/reset every Small Block Ticket to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Only Big Block Tickets issued after the previous big block are eligible for the draw.
Once the draw is complete, burn/reset every Big Block Ticket to 0.

The result is:
Small blocks remain extremely fair and fresh because no old tickets carry over.
Big blocks build up naturally, allowing people to watch their big block entries increase over weeks/months.
Metadata becomes very simple: display only the two counters plus permanent badges.

The triggers remain pool-based: the small block activates as soon as the small pool = exactly $2,500, and the big block activates when the big pool = exactly $100,000. Secondary royalties continue to fund the pools but do not generate tickets.
All other mechanics remain unchanged, including the auto $5 commission, assigning a random ticket to an existing NFT when no referral is used, manual claim, etc.
This approach should be simpler both to implement and to explain to users.
Apologies for changing direction again — once you confirm that this is cleaner for you as well, we’re 100% locked.

Thanks man!

value_updates.issuance_timing: Immediately when a mint uses the referral code
value_updates.eligibility_window: Only Small Block tickets issued after the previous Small Block draw are eligible for the current draw
value_updates.post_draw_action: Burn or reset every Small Block ticket to 0 after the draw

decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already records both ticket counters and permanent badges, so no additional metadata change is required.
The same-message MODIFY already records the Small Block trigger and royalty funding; ticket cohort and reset semantics are owned by the Small Block ticket lifecycle.
The client explicitly says the no-referral random ticket allocation remains unchanged, and the candidate already records that rule.
The ticket-lifecycle change does not alter the Big Block winner count, prize amount, or pool-balance trigger, which is already represented by the same-message MODIFY.
Secondary royalties remain enabled and continue funding the prize pools; the prohibition on generating tickets is represented by the ticket lifecycle Requirements.
The client explicitly states that manual claim remains unchanged.
The automatic $5 referral allocation is explicitly unchanged by the ticket-lifecycle adjustment.
The client explicitly preserves the automatic $5 commission, so the candidate remains valid unchanged.
The new ticket-cohort rule necessarily narrows the entries eligible for each random prize draw to tickets issued after the previous corresponding draw.
